data.change_summary: End-to-end audit of the feed → detritus → DOC → mineralization bookkeeping pathway. Traced all mass flows for N and C through feed inputs, consumer routing (shrimp/microfauna), death/senescence (C7), fine detritus dissolution, decomposer mineralization, and nitrification. No hidden sinks or double-counts were found in the existing implementation. Added doc comments documenting the C7 death/senescence interface on all routing functions (route_dead_shrimp_to_detritus, route_plant_loss_to_fine_detritus, route_algae_loss_to_fine_detritus). Added mass-flow context documentation to step_nitrogen_cycle. Documented the decomposer O2 simplification (mineralization uses DO as Monod modulator but does not debit O2 stoichiometrically) in both code and MASS_FLOW.md. Added 3 new integration tests: quantitative DOC pathway rate verification (dissolution rate × time matches DOC produced, decomposer consumption verified, per-tick conservation), algae loss conservation, and microfauna routing conservation. The documented mass-flow map (docs/MASS_FLOW.md) covers all pools, stoichiometric constants, conversion functions, flow pathways, execution order, and 7 explicitly named simplifications.
outstanding_risks: Decomposer mineralization does not debit O2 stoichiometrically (documented as Known Simplification #7 in MASS_FLOW.md). Background BOD provides aggregate coverage, but a future phase should add explicit O2 coupling (2.67 mg O2 per mg C remineralized) for accurate DO dynamics.

Microfauna reserve_g accumulates from retained share of ingestion but has no decay or starvation draw (Known Simplification #3). This acts as a small one-way N/C sink that is negligible in practice but would need closing for a fully mass-balanced microfauna model.
Shrimp reserve_g has no maintenance metabolism draw (Known Simplification #4). Reserve only depletes via reproduction funding or death transfer.
Pre-existing test failure: save_load_with_active_cycle_state fails due to floating-point divergence after serialization roundtrip. Not caused by this change.

steps.description: Read and trace all mass-flow pathways through nitrogen_cycle.rs (feed leaching, dissolution, decomposer mineralization, nitrification), shrimp.rs (consumer routing, death routing), microfauna.rs (consumer routing), plant_growth.rs (growth, senescence routing), algae_growth.rs (growth, loss routing), and engine.rs (Feed action handler). Verified no hidden sinks or double-counts exist.

Verified ownership boundaries: each transfer is represented once in the correct system. Feed → particulate_organics (engine.rs), leaching → fine_detritus (nitrogen_cycle hourly), dissolution → DOC/DON (nitrogen_cycle hourly), mineralization → TAN/DIC (nitrogen_cycle hourly), nitrification → NO2/NO3 (nitrogen_cycle hourly), consumer feeding → feces/excretion/respiration/retained (shrimp/microfauna daily), death → fine_detritus (shrimp/plant/algae daily), microbe decay → DOC/DON directly (nitrogen_cycle hourly).

Added doc comments on C7 death/senescence routing functions: route_dead_shrimp_to_detritus (shrimp.rs), route_plant_loss_to_fine_detritus (plant_growth.rs), route_algae_loss_to_fine_detritus (algae_growth.rs). Added mass-flow context documentation to step_nitrogen_cycle (nitrogen_cycle.rs) describing the hourly cascade and how C7 inputs join the same downstream path.

Documented decomposer O2 simplification: added inline comment in nitrogen_cycle.rs decomposer section noting that DO modulates rate via Monod factor but is not debited stoichiometrically, with background BOD providing aggregate coverage. Added Known Simplification #7 in docs/MASS_FLOW.md.

Added quantitative DOC pathway integration test (doc_pathway_quantitative_rates): Phase A verifies dissolution rate × time produces expected DOC (geometric decay of fine_detritus matches (1-r)^N, DOC produced matches dissolved × 1000/(1+ratio)). Phase B verifies decomposer consumption decreases DOC pool and increases TAN/DIC. Phase C verifies per-tick N and C conservation with both dissolution and consumption active.
Added algae_loss_enters_detritus_and_conserves integration test: verifies algae respiration + grazing loss produces fine detritus/DOC and conserves N and C over 120 hours.
Added microfauna_routing_conserves_with_feed integration test: verifies microfauna consumer routing conserves N and C per-tick over 120 hours with active detritus.
Verified all 11 feeding_detritus_audit tests pass, all 24 budget_tracking tests pass, cargo clippy clean, cargo fmt clean.

validation_evidence: cargo test --test feeding_detritus_audit: 11 passed, 0 failed (up from 8 original tests)
feed_pulse_nitrogen_conserved_over_120_hours: N conserved within 1e-6 mg tolerance over 120 hours in closed system with active biology
feed_pulse_carbon_conserved_over_120_hours: C conserved within 1e-6 mg tolerance over 120 hours
doc_pathway_quantitative_rates Phase A: fine_detritus geometric decay matches expected (1-0.08)^12, DOC produced matches dissolved × 1000/1.16 within 1e-6 mg
doc_pathway_quantitative_rates Phase B: decomposer consumption reduces DOC pool, increases TAN and DIC, N/C conserved within 1e-6 mg
doc_pathway_quantitative_rates Phase C: per-tick N and C balanced within 1e-6 mg with both dissolution and consumption active over 48 hours
death_derived_detritus_follows_same_downstream_path: feed-only and death-only scenarios produce identical DOC/TAN/DIC within 1e-9
shrimp_death_plus_feed_conserves_nitrogen: N and C conserved within 1e-6 mg with simultaneous feed processing and shrimp mortality over 120 hours
plant_senescence_enters_detritus_and_conserves: N and C conserved within 1e-6 mg over 120 hours with plant senescence
algae_loss_enters_detritus_and_conserves: N and C conserved within 1e-6 mg over 120 hours with algae loss
microfauna_routing_conserves_with_feed: per-tick N balanced within 1e-6 mg over 120 hours with active microfauna
Only pre-existing failure: save_load_with_active_cycle_state (serialization roundtrip floating-point drift, unrelated to mass balance)
